text: Q and P inputs contain only abstracts. Q says learning-augmented algorithms use fallible predictions while retaining formal guarantees and explicitly flags prediction cost, feedback, composition, endogenous error, semantic predictors, and benchmarking. P says its ray-tracing PPO policy reduces average MAE only about 3% versus the stronger mean-optimized geometric baseline, with gains up to about 14% on individual segments but comparable or slightly higher error elsewhere. This directly supports studying a reliability wrapper, but not yet identifying PPO itself as a formally defined prediction.

I reject the scan hypothesis as stated: neither abstract supplies Q theorem hypotheses/construction details nor P action space, GDOP objective, deployment loss, or a prediction-error definition. In particular, ray-tracing mismatch/campus shift does not by itself yield a deterministic prediction-error-dependent fallback bound. A claim that MARL is a fallible prediction and GDOP a robust fallback would therefore be an analogy, not a supported reduction.

Sharpened publishable line: treat MARL and mean-optimized GDOP as two candidate placements and learn a pre-deployment loss estimator/gate. If its per-candidate localization-loss estimates satisfy |Lhat(c)-L(c)|<=epsilon for c in {MARL,GDOP}, choosing argmin Lhat gives L(chosen)<=min{L(MARL),L(GDOP)}+2epsilon and hence <=L(GDOP)+2epsilon. A thresholded gate can retain exact GDOP worst-case robustness by deploying MARL only with a valid one-sided certificate; otherwise it falls back. The non-obvious research burden is to construct and empirically calibrate such certificates from ray-tracing/CIR features under segment shift, including prediction cost. P segment heterogeneity motivates the gate; Q motivates its guarantee axes. This is conditional and potentially publishable, but the elementary selector lemma alone is not.

Unresolved: obtain full papers and test whether P exposes a deployment-time surrogate or uncertainty score, whether GDOP has any formal worst-case localization bound under NLOS, and whether Q contains a construction whose hypotheses fit candidate selection. Without those, only the conditional 2epsilon selector theorem is supported, not the proposed hybrid robustness claim.

Cross-check confirms Emmy #1-#2. Q explicitly separates formal guarantees from empirical systems evidence and says only sufficient conditions permit limited end-to-end reasoning; P reports PPO is merely comparable on five campus segments, about 3% average MAE improvement, up to 14% on some segments, and slightly higher error on others. P also says its reward combines accuracy and coverage, whereas evaluation reports localization MAE. Thus neither the PPO output nor its reward is yet a prediction interface/error measure aligned to deployment loss, and GDOP is not stated to have a worst-case localization guarantee under NLOS.

Sharpen Emmy #3: uniform point estimates yield only the elementary +2epsilon selector guarantee, not exact fallback robustness. Exact no-worse-than-GDOP selection follows only when valid intervals are available and MARL is selected under U_MARL <= L_GDOP; then true L_MARL <= U_MARL <= L_GDOP <= true L_GDOP. Otherwise abstain to GDOP. With probabilistic interval coverage this is a high-probability guarantee, not deterministic; campus-segment shift threatens coverage/exchangeability and must be part of the theorem and experiments.

Verdict: reject the scan reduction as stated, but retain a conditional publishable line: selective, shift-aware certification for choosing between P-style MARL and GDOP placements. Define placement loss as downstream TDOA MAE (and impose coverage separately), learn paired loss intervals from CIR/ray-tracing features, choose MARL only on certified dominance, and otherwise use GDOP. Evaluate acceptance rate and realized gain versus certificate violation under ray-tracing mismatch and leave-one-campus-segment-out shift, while charging prediction cost as Q requests. Novelty must reside in finite-sample shift-aware interval validity plus useful MARL acceptance, not the selector lemma.

Publication support remains conditional because supplied inputs are abstracts only. Five segments are likely too few independent groups for strong segment-shift calibration, and P provides no uncertainty score, candidate action details, held-out protocol, or evidence that GDOP is a formally robust fallback. Calling fallback to GDOP worst-case robustness would overclaim: it only preserves the baseline choice, whose NLOS weakness P explicitly states.

Unresolved: full texts must establish Q construction hypotheses and P data splits/action space; additional campuses or many defensible shift units may be required; a certificate family valid under the intended ray-tracing mismatch must be specified. Concrete go/no-go test: intervals retain target coverage under held-out segment/site shift and certify MARL often enough to improve MAE after inference/simulation cost. If not, there is no supported learning-augmented result from this pair.

Refine Ada #7: exact baseline preservation does not require knowing true GDOP loss if one certifies the paired difference Δ(x)=L_MARL(x)-L_GDOP(x). Given an upper certificate UΔ(x) with simultaneous or marginal validity Δ(x)<=UΔ(x), deploy MARL only when UΔ(x)<=0; otherwise deploy GDOP. On the certificate-valid event, selected loss is no greater than GDOP loss. Equivalently, separate intervals require U_MARL<=lower_GDOP, not merely comparison to an unavailable true L_GDOP. This preserves the GDOP baseline decision, not worst-case localization robustness.

Final evidence-backed verdict: reject the abstract scan hypothesis as stated and sharpen it to selective, shift-aware baseline preservation. Q says learning-augmented algorithms use fallible predictions while retaining formal guarantees, separates formal guarantees from empirical systems evidence, and flags prediction cost, endogenous error, semantic predictors, and benchmarking. P says PPO uses ray-traced CIRs and a shared reward combining accuracy and coverage, but reports only ~3% average MAE gain over mean-optimized GDOP, up to ~14% on individual segments, with comparable or slightly higher error elsewhere. Thus heterogeneity motivates an abstaining selector, but MARL is an action policy—not yet Q-style prediction—and GDOP is explicitly propagation-blind, not a robust oracle.

Single publication candidate and go/no-go criterion: learn a finite-sample upper certificate for paired downstream loss difference Δ under explicitly defined ray-tracing mismatch/site shift, deploy MARL only when certified non-inferior (and coverage constraints pass), otherwise GDOP; report certificate coverage/violations, MARL acceptance, MAE gain, coverage, and prediction/simulation cost. Publication value must come from a defensible shift-valid certificate that accepts often enough for net gain. Five campus segments and abstracts alone do not support such a theorem; full data/protocols, more independent shift units, and Q construction hypotheses are unresolved. If target-shift validity or useful acceptance fails, conclude nothing publishable follows from this pair.

I accept Emmy #12 and correct my #7 formulation: define paired downstream loss difference Δ(x)=L_MARL(x)-L_GDOP(x), construct an upper certificate UΔ, and choose MARL only when UΔ<=0 (plus the separate coverage constraint). On the event Δ<=UΔ, this preserves the GDOP baseline decision without observing true GDOP loss. Separate candidate intervals would instead require U_MARL<=lower_GDOP. Neither statement makes GDOP itself worst-case robust under NLOS.

Final paired-paper result: reject the proposed MARL-as-prediction/GDOP-as-robust-fallback reduction, but support a concrete conditional research result—selective shift-aware baseline preservation. Q supplies the target structure (fallible prediction plus guarantees; prediction cost, endogenous/semantic error, benchmarking), while P supplies the empirical need: ray-traced PPO improves mean MAE only ~3%, reaches ~14% on some segments, and is comparable or worse on others. A finite-sample upper certificate for paired TDOA-MAE difference under a stated mismatch/shift class can gate MARL and otherwise abstain to GDOP. The publishable contribution must be shift-valid certification with nontrivial acceptance/net gain, not the elementary gating implication.

Remaining unresolved at handoff: the inputs are abstracts, so full papers/data must establish Q construction hypotheses and P action/data splits; the shift class and certificate method are unspecified; five segments may be insufficient independent calibration units; coverage must remain a separate feasibility constraint; prediction/ray-tracing cost must be charged. Go only if held-out site/mismatch validity is defensible and certified MARL acceptance produces net MAE benefit; otherwise the pair yields motivation but no publishable guaranteed hybrid.
